newsitem.title: FRANCE: France voices horror over bombing in Israel.
newsitem.headline: France voices horror over bombing in Israel.

text.p: France expressed horror on Friday after a suspected Moslem suicide bomber killed two people and wounded 43 in a cafe in Tel Aviv and urged all sides in the Middle East to work for a durable peace.
In a letter to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, President Jacques Chirac strongly condemned the attack, calling it a "cowardly and odious" act.
"I am convinced that this atrocious tragedy will not dissuade the Israeli and Palestinian people from the pursuit of peace, which is now more necessary than ever," Chirac said.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe denounced the "criminal act which struck at innocent victims" and echoed Chirac's call for peace in the region in a separate letter to Netanyahu.
"The horror of this attack must not deter those who are courageously pursuing the peace process," Juppe said.

The French foreign ministry earlier issued a statement condemning the attack and voiced concern over violence in Hebron and Jerusalem, where Palestinians are protesting against the construction of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"The French government learned with horror and consternation of the heinous attack that has just been committed in Tel Aviv. It expresses its sympathy to the families of the victims," the ministry said in a statement.
"The government also expresses its concern and dismay in light of the serious incidents in Jerusalem and Hebron," the statement said.

"It launches an appeal for reason to triumph over passion and for the avoidance of all acts, measures or remarks that could aggravate the situation and increase tension," the statement said. "The logic of peace and dialogue can and must triumph," it said.
